newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ backs PNG govt but opposes use of mercenaries.
newsitem.headline: NZ backs PNG govt but opposes use of mercenaries.

text.p: New Zealand backs the elected government of Papua New Guinea in its crisis with the military but remains opposed to its use of foreign mercenaries, Foreign Minister Don McKinnon said on Tuesday.
McKinnon was due to meet PNG's envoy to Wellington after news that the army chief, who earlier demanded the resignation of Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan, had now agreed to accept his own sacking.

Asked what message he would convey to PNG High Commissioner Damien Gamiandu, McKinnon said: "Obviously our concern for what has happened. Certainly our support that the democratic government does remain and does retain authority."

He said he would also express the hope that the crisis with the military would settle down and the view of countries in the region that "mercenaries from other parts of the world are not the most welcome individuals".

The current crisis was sparked when defence force commander Brigadier-General Jerry Singirok demanded Chan's resignation over a plan to use foreign mercenaries to quash a secessionist rebellion on the island of Bougainville.
McKinnon said he was concerned about the regional impact of the crisis in PNG.
"You have to be concerned about the overall effect on regional stability," he said.

"One hopes that cool heads have prevailed, that things will settle down. The army commander now knows he hasn't got a job. One hopes the rest of the military settle down and the issue of Bougainville can once again be addressed in a positive way."
McKinnon said New Zealand considered the situation to be calm and was not issuing any instructions to its 3,000 nationals in PNG. There was no immediate concern for their safety.
"But given what has happened in the last 24 hours you do have to remain a little bit uncertain, a little bit careful over the next few days." -- Wellington newsroom 64 4 473-4746
